They categorize tree conditions from A (highest priority) to D (lowest priority).  There isnât a set timeframe for work in category C. If the condition gets worse, please file a new request. Parks will reinspect the tree and update the priority level if needed. You can track the status of the work through the Tree Work Hub at nyc.gov/parks/treework.  If you prefer not to wait, you can hire a qualified tree care contractor. You'd need to pay for the work yourself and get a Tree Work Permit. You can apply for the free permit at nyc.gov/parks/trees.  Are you interested in caring for street trees in your neighborhood? You can get trained and certified by Trees New York to prune low-hanging branches. To learn about the free Citizen Pruner program, visit treesny.org/citizen-pruners-stewardship.

We will complete all work in Category A first and address work in lower priority categories in accordance with available resources. For more information about the Tree Risk Management Program, visit the NYC Urban Forest page on the NYC Parks website at nyc.gov/parks/trees.   Alternatively, you may choose complete the work yourself by hiring an independent contractor. The contractor must complete a Tree Work Permit application on the NYC Parks website at nyc.gov/parks/trees.
